text:
emily.h: Heads up — after the role_map refactor rolled last night I'm seeing cross-workspace project listings from the public GraphQL endpoint. @samir.k @jordan_sre can you take a look?

samir.k: confirm what you mean by "project listings" — is it metadata enumeration (names/ids) or actual access to resources?

emily.h: enumeration only so far — response contains projects from other orgs when a service account token is used with workspace header X-Workspace. quick repro attached below, it's just a curl.

emily.h: ```
curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer SA_TOKEN' -H 'X-Workspace: workspace-alpha' https://api.redwood.ai/graphql -d '{projects{ id name workspace }}'
```

jordan_sre: yikes. I see a spike in GraphQL ListProjects in prod around 03:12 UTC. Logs show the auth principal resolves to a service-account mapped to workspace-alpha but results include workspace-bravo ids.

mike-r: pulled a raw audit line: ```{"ts":"2026-02-14T03:12:22Z","principal":"sa:edge-sync","mapped_workspace":"workspace-alpha","endpoint":"/graphql","operation":"ListProjects","response_count":32,"projects_sample":[{"id":"proj-9b","workspace":"workspace-bravo"}]}```

sec-bot: Security alert created: SEQ-2026-022 - potential multi-tenant enumeration. Link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SEQ-2026-022

jordan_sre: mitigation plan: 1) throttle and deny enumeration for SA tokens without explicit cross-workspace grant 2) add a gateway-layer check that `response.projects.workspace == request.workspace` before returning lists. I can push a fast patch to the gateway to enforce the header check.

mike-r: rolling a canary blocker now — patch will drop list fields from GraphQL if workspace mismatch. Command I used: `kubectl -n api rollout restart deploy/graphql-gateway && kubectl patch networkpolicy gateway-policy --patch '{"spec":{"egress":...}}'` (shortened).

deploy-bot: deploy/graphql-gateway v2026.02.14-canary rolled to 3/10 pods at 03:19 UTC by mike-r :rocket:

samir.k: good. we also need to confirm KMS impact — does listing projects allow an attacker to enumerate keys or attempt decrypt? who owns KMS bindings? @mike-r @emily.h

emily.h: my read of key bindings: keys are bound to workspace IDs and require separate IAM assertions + kms:decrypt permission. But if attacker can enumerate project ids they can try to call KMS decrypt in a guessing attack.

sec-bot: quick query to check decrypt attempts run: `idx:kms_logs action:Decrypt AND principal:sa:* AND ts:[now-1h TO now]` — none in last 60m. Recommend increasing logging retention and running 24h window.

mike-r: running export of all ListProjects responses for the last 6 hours -> pushing to s3://redwood-security/repro/seq-2026-022/ for triage.

emily.h: can we export audit logs to SIEM and enable alerts for any KMS decrypts that originate from service accounts not bound to that workspace? That's the high-risk vector.

jordan_sre: agreed. Action items: (1) rollback role_map patch (emily.h) OR keep gateway check until we have a safe refactor (2) security to run KMS decrypt audit (samir.k) (3) export list responses + repro (mike-r) (4) update incident ticket with scope + owner + ETA 1h.

emily.h: I'll coordinate rollback to canary stage if gateway enforcement causes user visible issues. ETA 45m.

samir.k: on KMS audit, will check decrypt logs and key-binding table, will update SEQ-2026-022 within 30m.

mike-r: export done to s3, sharing presigned link in the ticket.

emily.h: thanks team — prioritize containment. post any suspicious decrypt attempts here. :eyes:
